Launcher guides

Check your Nintendo Switch playtime and see it on your PC

On your Switch or Switch 2, select your user icon on the HOME Menu and scroll down on your profile: it shows the playtime of the 20 games you played most recently. To bring Nintendo’s playtime into PlayCounter, open My Games, choose Nintendo and select Import from Nintendo.

By the PlayCounter project · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 steps

  1. Find hours on the console
  2. Find hours in Nintendo’s apps
  3. Import into PlayCounter
  4. How Switch hours add up
On this page
  • Find hours played on the Switch
  • Find hours in Nintendo’s apps
  • Import your Switch hours into PlayCounter
  • How Switch hours add up

Find hours played on the Switch

  1. On the HOME Menu, select your user icon (My Page).
  2. On the Profile page, scroll down.
  3. It lists the total playtime of up to 20 games you played most recently.

The steps are the same on a Nintendo Switch 2. A game that is not among those 20 is not listed, and the console needs an internet connection to show the latest play activity of your Nintendo Account.

Find hours in Nintendo’s apps

  • Nintendo Store app: open the User Page and tap Play Activity. It shows the games you played recently with the time per day, and All Activity can be sorted by Total Time Played. New play can take up to a day to appear. Nintendo 3DS and Wii U play is shown only up to February 2020.
  • Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app: with your console linked, Play Activity shows the daily play time and Monthly Summary the play time of each day in a month.

Import your Switch hours into PlayCounter

Worth doing once: signing in brings in the playtime Nintendo recorded for the games you played on your Switch, and PlayCounter keeps it up to date by itself.

  1. Open Nintendo in My Games

    In the sidebar under My Games, select Nintendo, then Import from Nintendo. After your first import, the button says Import more from Nintendo.

  2. Sign in

    Select Sign in and find games and sign in with Nintendo in the window that opens. At the end, Nintendo shows your account: choose Select this person. If Nintendo’s page does not work there, select Sign in with a link on the Launcher accounts page: sign in at Nintendo in your browser, right-click Select this person, copy the link and paste it.

  3. Review and import

    Nintendo’s games are found by their name. A game with one clear match waits in Ready to import. Games under Needs you ask you to pick the right game first, for example when two games share a name. Then select Import.

You sign in directly with Nintendo; PlayCounter does not see your password. The app keeps the sign-in on your PC, encrypted for your Windows account; Sign out on the Launcher accounts page deletes it. Your playtime stays on your PC: the PlayCounter API only receives game titles, as search queries, to find names and cover art. Import privacy details.

How Switch hours add up

Nintendo’s total is console play, so it never overlaps the sessions PlayCounter records on your PC: it is added to your PC time instead of compared with it. 40 hours on the Switch and 5 hours PlayCounter tracked on your PC show 45 hours.

While PlayCounter runs, it reads Nintendo’s list again about once an hour. A new game you play on your Switch shows up in My Games on its own when its name fits exactly one game. Nintendo can take up to a day to list new play, and there are no live Switch sessions: a Switch game does not appear in Now Playing while you play it. How launcher totals combine.
